tax.text: She voted against a budget proposal that paired large tax cuts with cuts to health care and other services.
tax.quote: This proposal will take away health care and other essential services from Americans

wages.text: She supported legislation to raise the federal minimum wage and said it should provide workers a living wage.
wages.quote: It’s time for Congress to stand up for working families and strengthen the middle class by raising the federal minimum wage.

trade.text: She called for repealing broad tariffs while supporting targeted trade policy.
trade.quote: We also need to repeal the president’s chaotic tariffs and ensure that trade policy is targeted and strategic moving forward.

debt.text: She introduced legislation to strengthen Social Security benefits and opposed proposals to weaken Medicare.
debt.quote: we should advance forward-looking reforms that strengthen the program and ensure all Americans can retire with dignity and economic security

housing.text: She supported a housing package intended to increase affordable-home supply and reduce barriers to building.
housing.quote: a comprehensive, bipartisan housing package that will boost affordable housing supply, modernize outdated federal programs, and cut unnecessary regulatory barriers so communities can build more homes.

schools.text: She backed a resolution supporting local public schools and opposing efforts to defund them, and cosponsored a bill to repeal the federal school voucher program.
schools.quote: The resolution highlights the historical role of the federal government in public K-12 education to promote equity of access for all students, regardless of background or ability.

safety.text: She supports funding community-based programs that aim to prevent gun violence and has backed legislation to increase police accountability.
safety.quote: Rep. DelBene supports increasing annual funding for frontline community-based organizations that are implementing evidence-informed intervention programs to prevent gun violence in America’s most impacted communities

immigration.text: She helped introduce legislation for an earned path to citizenship for people without criminal records.
immigration.quote: would create an earned path to citizenship for those who are here, working, and with no criminal record.

guns.text: She supports expanded background checks, an assault-weapons sales ban, and red-flag laws.
guns.quote: I support expanding background checks, banning the sale of semiautomatic assault weapons, and implementing extreme risk protection orders

abortion.text: She supported the Women’s Health Protection Act to protect abortion access and oppose state restrictions.
abortion.quote: The House and Senate must pass the Women’s Health Protection Act without delay so we can protect women from these terribly invasive state laws

gender.text: She helped reintroduce the Equality Act, which would add gender-identity protections in education.
gender.quote: would provide explicit, consistent civil rights protections for sexual orientation and gender identity in credit, education, employment, federal funding, housing, jury service and public accommodations.

cannabis.text: She supported the MORE Act to decriminalize marijuana federally and let states set their own marijuana policies.
cannabis.quote: The MORE Act is an opportunity to reinvest in these communities, expunge drug convictions to give people a second chance, and allow states to make the decisions that best serve their residents

health.text: She supports universal coverage through a choice between public and private coverage options.
health.quote: I support getting America to universal quality coverage and the best way to incentivize competition is to give people a choice between public and private coverage options.

energy.text: She backed clean energy investment and legislation intended to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
energy.quote: Our nation must take meaningful steps to build a new economy based on clean and renewable energy sources while we reduce our dependence on fossil fuels and foreign oil.

voting.text: She supports mail voting and opposed bills she said would disenfranchise eligible voters.
voting.quote: We must also protect mail-in voting because it is safe, secure, and legal.

tax.text: Silva said she would press states, including Washington, to change their tax systems and reduce the overall tax burden.
tax.quote: She said she would also pressure states like Washington to revamp their tax systems and reduce the overall tax burden.

immigration.text: She called for enforcing immigration law and securing the border, while also emphasizing assimilation.
immigration.quote: We must enforce the rule of law; an unsecure border undermines our entire system and places an involuntary burden on taxpayers.

energy.text: She favors removing regulatory barriers and relying on markets rather than regulations that shut down industries.
energy.quote: remove regulatory barriers, then free up the markets to innovate and solve these problems instead of shutting down industries.

voting.text: Her campaign platform calls for voter ID, and her voter-guide response calls for paper ballots counted at precinct level.
voting.quote: Require voter ID to guarantee secure, transparent, and trustworthy elections.
